t.E483.agn: In 2020 EFSA stated that adequate toxicity and genotoxicity data were not available and that data showing complete breakdown in the digestive tract were also lacking. It therefore reported that its safety could not be assessed and that the acceptable intake set by the SCF in 1978 could not be confirmed. The EU removed E483 from the list of authorised additives by Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/2379.
t.E483.body: It is not known to what extent stearyl tartrate is broken down and absorbed in the digestive tract or how it is processed in the body; the available data are not sufficient to show this.
t.E483.eff.0.t: Its safety could not be assessed because adequate toxicity and genotoxicity data were lacking; the EU removed it from the authorised list in 2023
t.E483.eval: No longer authorised as a food additive in the EU: it was removed from the authorised list by Regulation (EU) 2023/2379; it may not be used in foods placed on the market after 23 April 2024 (in 2020 EFSA found no data with which to assess its safety). The fatty acid source may also be animal.
t.E483.found.0: Not authorised in the EU since 2024
t.E483.prod: It is an emulsifier produced by esterifying tartaric acid with stearyl alcohol.
t.E483.regx.0: Re-evaluated; safety could not be assessed owing to insufficient data, previous acceptable intake could not be confirmed.
t.E483.regx.1: Removed from the EU list of authorised additives by Regulation (EU) 2023/2379; foods containing E483 may not be placed on the market after 23 April 2024, and those placed on the market before that date may be sold until the end of their shelf life.
t.E483.summary: An emulsifier produced from stearyl alcohol and tartaric acid. It is a dough improver in bakery products.
t.E483.what: It has been used as a dough improver and emulsifier in bakery products.
